notes: KX KDB HDB is a filesystem source and makes no HTTP requests.
Record mode exercises the deterministic temporary HDB contract.
q ground truth was recomputed on 2026-11-03 with the new runtime: per (date, sym) counts for all 4,938 dates and null counts for price, size and time on 64 sampled dates.
Every (date, symbol) row count in the destination table equals q's count of the HDB sym column, including rows whose symbol index is beyond the root sym file.

Full read on 0.1.17 into a fresh table: 5 batches, 22 min 15 s from update start to completion (20 min 44 s of flow time). The earlier single-batch build took about 23 minutes; 0.1.16, which probed each date serially through q, took 21 batches and about 68 minutes of batch time.
Header probes of older dates matched q's partition checks on 200 sampled dates (12 ms per date on 16 threads, against 268 ms per date through q).

With the default missing_columns=fail, the stream committed every date up to 2022.10.08 and then stopped at 2022.10.10, whose .d lists size without a size file. The full read used missing_columns=null.

End-of-day race test on a scratch copy of 2023.12.28-2023.12.30, run on 0.1.16 and again on 0.1.17: with only sym and time written for 2023.12.30 and no .d, an update committed no rows for that date; after price, size and .d were written, the next update appended exactly q's 3,495 rows.
install_kdb.sh --offline -y rejects a run without --b64lic/--k4b64lic, so the license stays on the installer command line.
